interpretation: Design inspirations, not sports-performance replication or a profit guarantee.

sources.title: Learning From Crowds
sources.use: Unequal annotator reliability motivates partial pooling instead of counting every opinion equally.
sources.difference: The paper infers latent labels; this experiment uses saved official-linked results in supervised fitting. It does not reproduce the paper's algorithm or empirical claims.

sources.title: A Generative Bayesian Model for Aggregating Experts' Probabilities
sources.use: Event-specific prior and relative expert information motivate a market offset with learned evidence coefficients.
sources.difference: Our inputs are directional picks, not expert probabilities. The exact softmax and shrinkage constants are a new project specification, not the paper's implemented model.

sources.title: A Heuristic for Combining Correlated Experts When There Are Few Data
sources.use: Estimating expert skill and dependence can itself increase error in small samples. Use shrinkage and a market-only control.
sources.difference: We do not estimate a full expert covariance matrix with only a few multi-author fixtures. Exact-document deduplication is not a general dependence correction.

sources.title: Probabilistic Opinion Pooling
sources.use: Shared versus private information and competence versus equal representation distinguish predictive aggregation from a fair vote.
sources.difference: General aggregation theory does not establish a sports betting advantage.
